key_insight: EyeRobot 2.0 shows that precise bimanual manipulation can be improved by actively steering gaze to the task-relevant 3D point, rather than relying on wrist cameras. By combining physical fixation with foveated processing, it focuses visual compute where it matters most.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of performing fine-grained manipulation without needing extra wrist-mounted cameras or heavy visual sensing setups. It aims to maintain precision while reducing sensing complexity and concentrating computation on the most important parts of the scene.
method: Uses a single stereo camera paired with two movable eye viewpoints that swivel to center on a chosen 3D fixation point.
Applies active visual fixation (AVF) so the robot physically attends to the object or region relevant to the manipulation task.
Processes the centered images foveally by allocating more visual tokens to the image centers, prioritizing task-relevant details.
impact: This approach can simplify robot perception hardware while improving manipulation accuracy on fine tasks. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights a practical path toward more efficient vision systems that combine active sensing with attention-like computation.
